geometry_edits.rationale: Convert the monolithic stepped stack into a split-wing dominant mass to introduce a clearer public threshold while preserving a single governing form.
Orient the split to support a frontage-facing opening and maintain the long-bar neighborhood character.
Introduce a measured interstitial gap so the access edge reads as a real public seam rather than a sealed face.
Add a courtyard macro in the ancestry of the dominant mass to create a usable void tied to the ground plane.
Promote the courtyard wrapper to root so the hall/mass remains in ancestry while the new public void becomes governing geometry.
Set a substantial courtyard margin so the open-space figure is clearly legible in plan and section.
Align the court opening to the program access side to convert the frontage into active public ground.

graph_edits.rationale: Replace the generic setback macro with a split-wing massing rule to introduce a clearer public threshold while preserving the dominant stepped datum.
Align the split to the frontage direction so the ground edge can read as an access seam rather than a sealed wall.
Create a measured interstitial opening that can operate as a public approach or entry court.
Add a courtyard wrapper in the ancestry of the dominant mass so the open space becomes a governing figure rather than a decorative subtraction.
Use a substantial margin to make the void legible as usable public space.
Open the courtyard toward the program access side so the frontage can become active ground edge.

rationale: The candidate is a coherent stepped block in all four views, and the parcel containment reads cleanly. However, it behaves mostly like a generic tiered extrusion: the dominant gesture is legible but the mass does not open toward the verified access edge with a meaningful public void, court, notch, or undercut. The blue frontage is answered by a sealed or semantically neutral face rather than an active ground threshold, which is a blocking problem for the neighborhood-living brief. The silhouette is acceptable as an inhabited step mass, but in this instance the stepping reads more as repetitive setback than as a program-bearing section with public ground consequence. It is therefore not program-fit hard pass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More campus/community-center scale and spread than this compact neighborhood-living brief; should not be copied as a multi-wing complex.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Low-rise terraced composition with a central open space and connected wings; useful as a precedent for preserving one dominant mass while carving a legible public void.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Primarily a pavilion/restaurant object and not a stepped mass; transfer the threshold logic, not the building type.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple low-rise frontage with a clear entry setback and a calm roofline; good for active ground edge and compact street-building proportions.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Too facade-specific and image-only; no strong massing principle beyond a conventional shopfront threshold.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Street-facing low-rise commercial box with canopy/awning and glazed edge can inform an active frontage response.

warnings: Parcel containment is satisfied, but access-edge response is weak and should be corrected in the next iteration.
The form is coherent across views, so the main issue is semantic/sectional program fit rather than geometry stability.
Need a more legible public threshold aligned to the blue frontage; a courtyard, notch, split, or ground seam would be more appropriate than more generic tiering.
